findings.title: Require manage scope for global group management
findings.body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE, so an administrator granted only view permission on all groups passes requireManage(). GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup uses that check to authorize both creating groups and moving an existing subgroup to the top level. This gives a read-only administrator write access to the group hierarchy. Only MANAGE should satisfy this check; add a test that a VIEW-only grant cannot POST groups.

findings.title: Return model group IDs rather than authorization resource IDs
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() enumerates authorization resources and passes/returns groupResource.getId(), but these IDs are not GroupModel IDs: AdminPermissionsSchema creates a resource with a generated ID and stores the model group ID in its name. hasPermission() subsequently looks up by name, and UsersResource uses the returned set to filter users by group membership. In particular, with an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS grant this enumerates the synthetic Groups resource and returns its authorization ID, causing user searches to filter on a nonexistent group and return no members. Individual resources also are not assigned a Groups type by getOrCreateResource(), so this enumeration does not discover them. Resolve actual group IDs, handle the all-groups grant explicitly, and test user search/count with both individual and all-groups member permissions.
